analysis.title: "Priced For Perfection": BTIG Says Refiners' Worst Day Since Liberation Day Is The "Start Of The Unwind"
key_insights: BTIG chief technical strategist Jonathan Krinsky is pressing a cautious view on refiners. He was early in mid-September, reiterated in mid-October, and now says to press the view after the group fell almost 7% in one session on Tuesday 10/27.

The S&P 500 Refining & Marketing index was up 157.3% YTD through 10/26, the best calendar year in at least three decades by nearly 2x. The prior best years were 2012 (+80.1%) and 2005 (+77.3%). Krinsky expects at minimum consolidation and more likely significant downside reversion.

The refiners index was down 6.8% intraday on Tuesday, its worst day since Liberation Day (April 2025). The index is up about 300% since then. The drop came on a day the S&P 500 was up from record highs, which Krinsky reads as a possible first crack in a crowded trade rather than capitulation.

The 3-2-1 crack spread has fallen from a peak of roughly $70/bbl in September (ZH's read off the chart) to about $51, a breakdown toward multi-month lows. Refiner equities kept climbing until about two weeks ago, so they priced record margins as margins rolled over.

The Nymex gasoline crack fell to $27.94/bbl on Friday, its lowest since April, while the diesel crack was near $98, about 3.5x the gasoline margin. Gasoline is two-thirds of the 3-2-1 barrel, and US pump demand is down about 2% y/y per Goldman nowcasts. Refinery utilization is at its highest since 1998.
Other margin headwinds cited: the first Russian diesel tanker sailing for the US under the Trump-Moscow fuel deal, and diesel export ban chatter out of Washington.

Chart signals: CRAK (VanEck Oil Refiners ETF) is cracking support. Valero (VLO) was down nearly 7% at one point and is breaking its steep uptrend in place since June, less than a week after $6.8B Q3 net income ($23.89/share). Marathon Petroleum (MPC) is still above its uptrend line but is 'starting to act tired'.

Energy (XOP) is failing at the upper end of its trend channel. Krinsky sees risk back toward the uptrend line around $186 with XOP near $200, a roughly 7% downside. Energy was the worst-performing sector on Tuesday.

Breadth: SPX rose on negative breadth again Tuesday. SPX price and breadth have moved in opposite directions on 33% of trading days this year, the most of any year since at least 1996. Rates were down, crude was down and tech led, which would normally suggest broadening into cyclicals, but breadth stayed negative.

Krinsky argues energy falling is more likely the start of a correlated downside move than an SPX breakout. Energy has acted as ballast against AI-stock wobbles, and removing that offset opens the path to a 'correlation-one' 80%+ downside volume day.

Krinsky is skeptical of the consensus post-midterm rally trade (note: 'Midterms Unlikely a Clearing Event'), saying there is far too much optimism given there was no pre-midterm selloff in the S&P 500.

Mizuho moved to the sidelines on Phillips 66 (PSX), Delek and Par Pacific on Oct 8 while raising refiner price targets about 40% on average. The group had about 4% average upside left, trading at roughly 8.5x two-year forward EV/EBITDA versus a 6.7x historical average.

ZH's view: physical product markets remain tight (refinery outages above Goldman's prolonged-disruption scenario, hub inventories at lows, a maintenance wall in Q2 2027), but the refiner stocks can fall regardless because a 157% gain already discounts more than tightness.

sector_views.rationale: BTIG's Krinsky is cautious: +157% YTD is the best year in three decades, the crack spread is rolling over from about $70 to about $51, and charts are breaking trend.
XOP is failing at the top of its channel with roughly 7% downside to about $186, and energy falling may begin a correlated broad market downside move.

earnings_insights: Valero reported Q3 net income of $6.8 billion, or $23.89 a share (reported, already printed, less than a week before 10/27). The stock was nonetheless breaking its uptrend after the print.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Blended refining margin is 25%-30% off highs, a breakdown toward multi-month lows, which pressures refiner earnings expectations.
Lowest since April, and the weak leg of the 3-2-1 spread.
About 3.5x the gasoline margin, still a crisis level, but diesel is only one-third of the 3-2-1 barrel.

macro_indicators.reading: down about 2% y/y per Goldman nowcasts
macro_indicators.interpretation: Weak pump demand drags the gasoline leg and the blended margin.

risk_factors: Diesel could stay in crisis into 2027 and keep the physical market tight, which could support refiners despite the call.
Krinsky's call was early in mid-September and the stocks rose another few dozen percent afterward, so timing risk is high.
A rotation out of energy into the rest of the market could instead push the S&P to a breakout, the bulls' counter.
Product market tightness: refinery outages above Goldman's worst case, hub inventory lows, and a Q2 2027 maintenance wall.

vol_and_positioning: Refiners are described as the most crowded energy trade of the year. The group had its worst day in 18 months on Tuesday.
SPX price and breadth moved in opposite directions on 33% of trading days this year, the most since at least 1996.
The refiners index was 43% above its 200-day moving average in August, a level it has not spent much time above in the last 15 years.
Krinsky flags risk of a 'correlation-one' downside day (80%+ downside volume) with energy no longer offsetting tech weakness.
geopolitical: The Iran war, which has made energy the market's best hedge all year.
The first Russian diesel tanker sailing for the US under the Trump-Moscow fuel deal.
Diesel export ban chatter out of Washington.
G7 emergency fuel release in early October that barely dented the diesel crack.
cross_bank_references: Mizuho moved to the sidelines on Phillips 66, Delek and Par Pacific on Oct 8 while raising refiner price targets about 40% on average.
Goldman's nowcasts show US pump demand down about 2% y/y.

tension_points.bull_case: Physical product markets remain tight: refinery outages above Goldman's prolonged-disruption scenario, hub inventories at lows, a maintenance wall in Q2 2027, and diesel in crisis well into 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: The stocks are up 157% YTD and priced for perfection, the blended crack is 25%-30% off highs with gasoline at its weakest since April, and charts in VLO, CRAK and XOP are breaking trend.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break of the uptrend line in MPC would confirm the bearish view, while the bear case is weakened if the crack spread recovers toward its September peak near $70/bbl.

tension_points.bull_case: Money rotating out of energy goes into everything else and pushes the S&P to a breakout.
tension_points.bear_case: Energy has been the ballast, and its decline removes the offset, opening a path to a correlated 80%+ downside volume day.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Breadth turning positive with cyclicals participating on days when rates and crude fall and tech leads would undercut the correlated-downside thesis.

theme_stances.key_argument: Refiners are priced for perfection after a 157% YTD gain while crack spreads are rolling over, so consolidation or significant downside reversion is likely.
Energy falling is more likely the start of a more correlated downside move than an SPX breakout.
